articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 28: Need a defense as the Vikings head to Detroit? Get the Jags

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

We're officially entering the week where the No. 1 D/ST, the Minnesota Vikings (12.3 fantasy points per game, plus-2.8 over the next-closest team and plus-6.9 versus the league's average) face the toughest schedule-adjusted matchup in the Detroit Lions. And it's a road game, no less. Anyone care to guess the last time a visiting D/ST scored in double digits at Ford Field? It was the Green Bay Packers (10 fantasy points), back in Week 12 of 2023. Since then, only these same Vikings (9, Week 9 of 2025) and Tampa Bay Buccaneers (7, Week 7 of 2025) have scored as many as five points there.

It's remarkable that in this topsy-turvy NFL season -- the Cleveland Browns are division leaders and the Los Angeles Chargers and RB Omarion Hampton are off to a disastrous start, for two obvious examples -- that Week 8 presented perhaps my fewest Vampire league lineup dilemmas thus far.

Humble brag: Perhaps that's the result of my four-game winning streak, bolstering the roster with claims of Bhayshul Tuten, Bijan Robinson, Nico Collins and Jameson Williams. (On that note, sarcastic "thanks" to the manager who sat all his stars to protect any being claimed last week -- except Williams. You know who you are!)

But even putting those aside, only one lineup spot stood out and perhaps it's one that has been a frustrating spot to manage for many of you: Team defense/special teams.

Managers of the Vikings D/ST face a pair of decisions: Keep them around, or which unit to pick up as a substitution?

As far as the former, it doesn't get much easier for the Vikings over the coming weeks, much as they're a supremely talented defense. After the Lions game, the Vikings' remainder of November goes like this: BUF (on Monday Night Football), @GB, @SF (on Sunday Night Football), ATL. Using past-five-weeks, schedule-adjusted data, those are the Nos. 16, 18, 24 and 31 offenses for D/STs in terms of matchups. (The Buffalo Bills, by the way, are 27th if using full-season data, and the Green Bay Packers are 24th.)

I have no qualms about releasing a D/ST with a bad matchup, and that's any defense, though it'd be understandable if the only ones you're avoiding as a Vikings manager are the two Lions games (Week 15 at home is the other) and Bills. If you've got the bench space -- not an easy thing in these four-team bye weeks -- by all means keep them around. But you've got my permission slip to cut them otherwise.

articles.headline: Mussolini's great-grandson scores first goal for Lazio
articles.description: Romano Floriani Mussolini, the great-grandson of former Italian dictator Benito Mussolini, scored his first goal for Lazio on Tuesday.
articles.headlineJa: ムッソリーニのひ孫、ラツィオで初ゴールを決める
articles.descriptionJa: イタリアの元独裁者ベニート・ムッソリーニのひ孫であるロマーノ・フロリアーニ・ムッソリーニが、火曜日にラツィオで自身初となるゴールを決めた。
articles.body:
Romano Floriani Mussolini, great-grandson of the former fascist Italian dictator Benito Mussolini, scored his first goal for Lazio on Tuesday.

The 23-year-old Floriani Mussolini -- who has "Romano" on the back of his jersey -- struck in the 16th minute for Lazio's third goal in its 6-2 rout of Sassuolo in Serie A.

His celebrations were initially cut short by the offside flag, but the Lazio youth product managed to celebrate properly when the goal was given on video review.

It was also Mussolini's first goal in the Italian top flight and only the second of his career. His first had come in the second-division, two years ago, while on loan at Juve Stabia.

The defender, whose full name is Romano Benito Floriani Mussolini, is related to Benito Mussolini through the maternal side of his family.

He is the son of Alessandra Mussolini, a former member of the European parliament for the Forza Italia party.

He has said publicly that he has no interest in politics.

Mussolini was prime minister of Italy from 1922 to 1943 following a fascist coup in the country.

articles.body:
It's Week 8 of the 2026 NFL season, and we're under two weeks away from the trade deadline. Insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been calling sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

Which teams are most likely to bring in help before the Nov. 10 deadline? Which players are likeliest to end up in a new city? And will the Colts continue dealing players? Jeremy and Dan have updates on the trade market. Plus, we look into what's happening with the struggling Jets and what's going on in the chaotic AFC North, where the Browns are in first and the Ravens are in last.

It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 8.

Jump to:

Aggressive teams at the deadline

Players likely to move | Colts dealing

Jets changes | AFC North chaos

Fantasy advice | More intel

Which team is most likely to be aggressive in acquiring help at the deadline?

Fowler: The Chiefs appear poised to do something at wide receiver. Injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton have created holes in the passing game that running back Kenneth Walker III can't mask alone. The Chiefs have managed to win games despite those injuries, but Sunday night in Seattle was a reminder of how ugly things can look without adequate downfield playmakers.

Enough receivers will be available in the coming weeks, so the Chiefs can get good value trading for the high-impact players or lower-cost options. The Colts' Josh Downs would be a fit for the Chiefs. The Browns' Jerry Jeudy would also fit, though Cleveland is not inclined to deal him now barring a significant offer.

Graziano: The Chiefs always seem to do something at wide receiver at the deadline. Usually it's a smaller move such as Kadarius Toney or late-career DeAndre Hopkins, but the team has a history of targeted trade-deadline additions at the position. I expect Kansas City to be active in trying to add a player or two to boost the offense, be that another pass catcher, an offensive lineman or both.

The teams that are most interesting to me are the surprises. Would the first-place Giants believe they're in position to trade a draft pick or two for a win-now player? Would the AFC North-leading Browns feel compelled to reward their current roster for its surprising first-half success by adding a player who can help take them to the next level? We saw the Colts do this last year with the big swing for Sauce Gardner.

articles.headline: Fantasy Hoops: The Timberwolves players to add in wake of Anthony Edwards injury
articles.description: The Timberwolves to add as Anthony Edwards' injury opens up a lot of minutes and opportunity for teammates.
articles.body:
Minnesota Timberwolves guard Anthony Edwards was putting up some of the best numbers of his career before Tuesday's news. Through four games, he averaged 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds and 3.5 assists while shooting 48% from the field. He even scored 47 points in 41 minutes against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday despite dealing with knee pain.

Now Edwards is scheduled for arthroscopic surgery on his right knee Thursday and could miss around two months. A more definitive return timeline should come after the procedure. Edwards missed a career-high 21 games last season while dealing with knee issues, so managers should make every effort to stash him, even in leagues without an injured reserve spot.

LaMelo Ball should see the biggest increase in offensive responsibility. The offense will run through him more often, giving him additional opportunities to score and create for teammates. Ball's usage and assist potential should increase, although opposing defenses can now devote more attention to stopping him.

Jaden McDaniels should also see more shots, while Jonathan Kuminga (rostered in 54.6% of ESPN leagues) could take on additional scoring responsibility. Kuminga has averaged 11.5 PPG, 5.8 RPG and 2.0 SPG in 29.8 MPG this season. I like him more in points leagues because his free throw shooting can hurt teams in category-based formats.

Ayo Dosunmu (63.4% rostered) is the first player I'd check on the waiver wire. He's the favorite to move into the starting lineup and averaged 18.7 points and 7.3 rebounds in nine starts for the Wolves last season. Dosunmu averaged 33.5 minutes in those starts. Even if he doesn't reach those marks, a significant increase in playing time would make him worth rostering in all formats.

Terrence Shannon Jr. (8.7%) is another priority, particularly in 12-team leagues. He's averaged 13.0 PPG and 2.5 triples in just 22.3 MPG through four games. More playing time could make him a reliable source of scoring and 3-pointers. Bones Hyland (1.0%) is worth considering in leagues with 14 or more teams. He averaged 11.8 PPG, 3.3 APG and 2.3 triples across 20 games without Edwards last season, although his minutes aren't guaranteed.

To bring everything together, Dosunmu should be the top priority on waivers, followed by Kuminga, then Shannon in 12-team leagues, and Hyland in deeper formats.

articles.headline: LeBron, Durant headline NBA draft classes of the early 2000s
articles.description: The aughts are over? Here's a look at the players who remain from the early 2000s draft classes.
articles.body:
LeBron James is in a class of his own across many statistical categories in the league.

The Philadelphia 76ers forward has played the most seasons in NBA history (24 and counting). He boasts the most points and games played in the regular season (43,489, 1,625) and playoffs (8,521, 302). His 22 NBA All-Star appearances are the highest total of any player. Therefore, it's no secret that James, who faces the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday (7 p.m. ET on ESPN), is the last remaining player from his draft class -- 23 years ago.

The Cleveland Cavaliers selected James at No. 1 in 2003. He has since stood the test of time and then some. Of the top five players taken in that draft, the closest player to James' career length is Carmelo Anthony, who retired in May 2023 -- the same year James competed in the Western Conference finals. 

With Kyle Lowry retiring in the offseason, the league's remaining active players from drafts of the early 2000s are dwindling. Lowry was the last one left from a 2006 draft that included Rajon Rondo, Lamarcus Aldridge, Rudy Gay and current Lakers head coach JJ Redick. 

With Chris Paul's retirement in February, no one is left from the 2005 class. Aside from LeBron, there are no active players left from the 2000-2004 classes, either.    

Here's a look at the players who remain from the 2007 to 2010 classes.

Year:

  2007

Players: 

Kevin Durant (No. 2), Al Horford (No. 3), Mike Conley (No. 4)

All active players from this class are top-five picks. Two of the three are champions and made at least five All-Star appearances: Durant (16) and Horford (5). 

Durant's longevity stands out in this group. He averaged 26 points, 5.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists in the 2025-26 season, earning All-Star honors and making the All-NBA second team. Durant also played 78 games, his most since the 2018-19 campaign. 

Jeff Green, selected at No. 5 in 2007, finished his 20th NBA season last year while playing for the Houston Rockets. He remains a free agent, and has not made any retirement announcement. 

Year:

2008

Players:

Brook Lopez (No. 10), DeAndre Jordan (No. 35)

The 2008 class is hanging on with two big men still contributing. The LA Clippers picked up Lopez's option in June after he played 75 games and averaged 8.5 points and 3.6 rebounds last season. Jordan returned to the New Orleans Pelicans after being named the Twyman-Stokes Teammate of the Year. He appeared in just 12 games last year.  

However, this class lost some headliners in the offseason.

Russell Westbrook (No. 4) and Nicolas Batum (No. 25) each announced their retirements. Westbrook was the group's leader in minutes, games, points and assists and is bound for the Hall of Fame. Batum was one of the NBA's best role players. Kevin Love (No. 5) and Eric Gordon (No. 7) are still free agents and their careers remain up in the air.

2009

Players: 

James Harden (No. 3), Stephen Curry (No. 7), DeMar DeRozan (No. 9), Jrue Holiday (No. 17)

articles.headline: Man United's Michael Carrick and Bruno Fernandes hold 'clear-the-air' talks - reports
articles.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes have held clear-the-air talks.
articles.body:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick and captain Bruno Fernandes have held clear-the-air talks.

The Press Association understands Carrick and Fernandes met at United's Carrington training ground for talks that were separate to a wider meeting of the full squad to discuss a way forward from their current predicament.

Fernandes appeared to question Carrick's tactics in the wake of last week's 4-1 Champions League loss to Como, and was dropped for Sunday's Premier League match at home to Bournemouth, remaining on the bench throughout as United fell to stunning 3-0 loss that piled the pressure on Carrick.

However, after the talks, Fernandes is now considered available for the crunch match away to Chelsea on Saturday.

Fernandes, who lately has looked a shadow of the player of who was named the PFA Players' player of the year last term, is described as being back to the best version of himself over the past 48 hours following a difficult period on and off the pitch.

Sunday's result left United down in 16th place in the Premier League with only one league win -- over newly-promoted Ipswich -- this term.

Many observers had expected the axe to fall on the boss in the wake of Sunday's defeat, but Carrick took training on Tuesday with the club resolving to give the 45-year-old more time to turn things around.

Fernandes was the second player to make outspoken comments in a post-match interview in the space of two weeks, with Lisandro Martínez having taken aim at the club's hierarchy in an explosive interview following the 2-0 Champions League loss to Atlético Madrid on Oct.13.

Carrick took charge of the team in January, stabilising the club after Ruben Amorim's often turbulent reign, overseeing an excellent run of results which culminated in a third-placed finish and a return to the Champions League.

The popular former United midfielder was rewarded with a two-year deal in the summer, but just five months after signing it he has come under major scrutiny with United having won only two of their 12 matches in all competitions, those against Ipswich and Champions League minnows Sabah.

articles.headline: LaLiga chief Javier Tebas holds talks with Chinese ambassador over Mbappé-Mao controversy
articles.description: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has met with China's Ambassador to Spain, Yao Jing, to "find solutions" to the Kylian Mbappé alleged dictator comment.
articles.body:
LaLiga president Javier Tebas has met with China's Ambassador to Spain, Yao Jing, to "find solutions" to the Kylian Mbappé alleged dictator comment.

Comments made by the Real Madrid striker regarding a "meme" comparing him to Mao Zedong, the founder of the People's Republic of China, sparked controversy in the Asian country.

EFE reported that Chinese state broadcaster CCTV suspended evening broadcasts of LaLiga matches and any games involving Mbappé.

"Today I held a meeting with the Chinese Ambassador to Spain to discuss the situation arising from Kylian Mbappé's comments and to seek solutions to move past this incident," Tebas wrote on X.

"Over recent years, LaLiga has worked closely with the Chinese authorities, football organisations, broadcasters and businesses in the country to promote the growth and popularity of Spanish football in China, while also contributing to the development and growth of Chinese football itself by sharing our experience, expertise and resources."

 

LaLiga has partnership deals with different Chinese organisations, including a strategic agreement with the Chinese Professional Football League (CFL) through 2029.

Moreover, it has agreements with China Media Group (CMG) for the growth of Chinese football and to bring "our competitions closer to millions of fans."

Tebas said he hopes the "single incident" does not affect their rapport.

"This is a relationship built on mutual respect, trust and cooperation, which we must preserve and continue to strengthen," Tebas wrote. "We are committed to continuing to work together to ensure that a single incident does not undermine the significant progress made or affect the millions of Chinese fans who follow our competitions. China is, and will continue to be, a strategic partner for LaLiga."

- Kylian Mbappé dropped by Chinese brands after alleged dictator comment

- Why Real Madrid's Mbappé, Barcelona's Yamal lost Ballon d'Or

- If Clásico win is any indication, Mourinho's Madrid might just be special again

At least three companies have cut ties with the France and Madrid star since his comment.

Mbappé issued an apology to the Chinese people on Tuesday on his social media, stating that his comment regarding Mao Zedong was "ill-judged."

Real Madrid, who own a percentage of Mbappé's image rights, also joined their player in apologising to the Chinese people.

"Real Madrid C.F. wishes to express its apologies to the Chinese people for any discomfort that may have been caused by the recent words of our player Kylian Mbappé," a club statement said on Wednesday.

"Our club holds deep respect for China, its history, its culture, and its citizens, as well as for the millions of Chinese fans who feel affection and admiration for Real Madrid."

articles.headline: Barcelona fined €602 over Julián Álvarez approach
articles.description: Barcelona have been fined €602 ($669) by the Royal Spanish Football Federation [RFEF] for approaching Julián Álvarez before notifying Atletico Madrid of their interest.
articles.body:
Barcelona have been fined €602 ($669) by the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) for approaching Julián Álvarez before notifying Atlético Madrid of their interest.

Barça plan to appeal the decision, a source said.

The Spanish champions made several attempts to sign Álvarez in the summer as they sought a new striker to replace the outgoing Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

Their pursuit of the Argentina forward angered Atlético, who accused Barça of making an illegal approach for the player and subsequently reported them to both the RFEF and FIFA.

FIFA declared it had no jurisdiction over the case, but the RFEF announced a small fine this week after finding Barça made contact with Álvarez's agent at the time, Fernando Hidalgo, before Atlético.

The RFEF's investigation established that a conversation took place between Hidalgo and Barça sporting director Deco on May 15, with the Catalan club's first written communication with Atlético following on May 28.

However, the infringement was only considered a "minor regulatory breach," with it falling under Article 133 -- instead of Article 93 -- of the RFEF's Disciplinary Code and, therefore, carrying a smaller punishment.

Article 93 is applied for "conscious and repeated breaches" of the RFEF's regulations.

Barça offered €100 million ($111m) for Álvarez and left the offer on the table until the end of the transfer window, but Atlético CEO Miguel Ángel Gil Marín repeatedly insisted they would not sell to their LaLiga rivals.

Atlético also turned down a €150m ($166m) offer from Real Madrid for Álvarez during the summer, with Arsenal and Paris Saint-Germain also expressing an interest in signing the forward.

Álvarez had revealed a desire to leave, telling ESPN during the World Cup that he felt a transfer would be best for all parties. Sources told ESPN he wanted to join Barça.

His push for a transfer saw him booed by Atlético fans at the start of the season, although bridges have started to be mended in recent weeks.

The 26-year-old has scored in each of Atlético's last two games, against Stuttgart and Deportivo A Coruña, and after netting the winner in a 1-0 win against the latter on Saturday, he apologised to supporters.

"I wanted to say sorry to our fans for my comments during the World Cup," he told Movistar of his decision to speak out in search of a move.

"It was ‌a ⁠mistake -- the way I said what I said and the timing. I understand why the supporters are angry. If I were a fan, I'd be angry too. Especially given how they've supported me since I arrived."

Atlético have won eight of their opening 10 LaLiga games and are second in the table, just two points behind leaders Barcelona.

articles.headline: Arteta, Alonso, Iraola: Three Premier League managers all come from one tiny club
articles.description: Whether it be the Premier League, Champions League or World Cup, hiring a coach from Spain's northern coast is bringing clubs guaranteed success.
articles.headlineJa: アルテタ、アロンソ、イラオラ：プレミアリーグの3監督がすべて同じ小さなクラブ出身
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグ、チャンピオンズリーグ、あるいはワールドカップであれ、スペイン北岸出身のコーチを起用することは、クラブに確実な成功をもたらしている。
articles.body:
There is irresistible evidence right now that signing coaching talent from Spain's northern coast brings guaranteed success, and Arsenal, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Chelsea need no convincing.

In international terms, the European and world champions (Spain) are coached by a Basque (Luis De La Fuente), in club terms, double Champions League winners PSG dance to the tune of another north-coast Spaniard, Luis Enrique, and the reigning Europa League holders and English champions owe their success to a couple of guys, Unai Emery and Mikel Arteta, who grew up within a few miles of one another in San Sebastián (part of the Gipuzkoa territory in Spain's Basque country).

It is, literally, a phenomenon. This is a coaching domination by a small community on a grand scale.

Now the fascinating prospect is that four of England's great clubs will all be jostling for trophies and bragging rights this season, in the Premier League and in Europe, under the control of coaches who all learned at one amateur Gipuzkoa football club on the Bay of Biscay coastline.

Arteta, Emery, Andoni Iraola and Xabi Alonso have already enjoyed jaw-dropping coaching success -- historic triumphs with Arsenal, Bournemouth, Bayer Leverkusen, Sevilla and Aston Villa between them. Now, they will all be going toe-to-toe for England's silverware.

What they also share, particularly Arteta, Iraola and Alonso, is an identical development path, often criss-crossing experiences in their home town of San Sebastián, being trained under the same ethos, often by the same coaches.

The amateur club in question is Antiguoko, which can claim partial responsibility for Bournemouth earning their first ever UEFA qualification (Iraola played for Antiguoko as a kid then, eventually, began his coaching career there), for Bayer Leverkusen winning their only Bundesliga title (Alonso) and for Arteta bringing Arsenal their first Premier League trophy in 22 years. Remarkable, right?

Those who run football at Antiguoko, and around the Gipuzkoa region, are beginning to smile with resignation as Europe's media approach them and demand the magic formula which has produced these brilliant alumni (and a host of other key figures in coaching and directorial roles around the continent).

There's no magic -- just ideology, hard work, decades of development and attention to detail.

Iraola says: "The number of successful coaches formed in the Basque Country receives a lot of attention because, despite being a small place, we have a great football culture."

When Arteta was last asked about what it is that makes Basque coaches so successful he gave a simple, short answer: "It's about passion we have and the education that we all got."

That education includes the fact that kids who follow the Arteta-Alonso-Iraola route in Gipuzkoa, aren't allowed to belong to a single club, practising a single sport, until they're 10 years or older.
